stock_vllm_estimate._method: cachesave/stockvllm.py: stock prefix-cache rules for this hybrid model (whole blocks, GDN state only at each prompt's last full block, MTP drops the last block of a hit; no RAM tier, no tail reuse), LRU at 140,000 tokens (16-bit KV on a 32 GB card), same 1,237 requests. Calibration: the same model with our 3,200-token blocks and 480k cache gives 53.7 % vs our measured 62.3 % (RAM tier + tail reuse ~5 pts), so it may undercount by ~3 pts.

agent_replay._method: cachesave/stockvllm_range.py: 17,616 routed production requests 2026-11-03 17:21 - 2026-11-11 10:00 (RTX 5090 17,411, Arc 205), same replay for both sides: stock vLLM prefix-cache rules (832-token blocks, GDN state only at prompt ends, MTP drops the last block, 140k-token 16-bit KV per GPU, LRU, no RAM tier, no tail) vs ours (3,200-token blocks + token-exact tail hold, int4 KV at today's production sizes: RTX 5090 439,476 / Arc 482,846 tokens, LRU); wait = prefill seconds for the recomputed part on the measured cold-prefill curve; modeled, not timed; rerun 2026-11-13 (same window and requests; a rerun at the old 480k reproduces the 11-11 output exactly)

gpu_prefill_h._note: all 17,616 routed requests: sum of modeled prefill seconds (agent mean x n + vision mean x n); RAM-tier loads (PCIe, GPU keeps decoding) counted as recompute for ours, so ours is an upper bound

stall_on_others_agent_h._note: sum over requests of modeled prefill wait x other requests in flight on the same GPU at its start (router trace start/finish); assumes the others' decode stops while a prefill runs

task_replay._method: cachesave/tasksim.py: 340 multi-agent production tasks (router root conversation, 2+ agents), event-driven replay keeping each agent's outside-world gaps from the trace; prefill = per-request modeled wait (stock vs ours cache rules) x engine prefill factor, exclusive, pauses decode; decode = completion tokens at agg(n)/n of each engine's curve; metric = time with any of the task's requests in flight (union). Rerun 2026-11-13: engine curves = 5090 g5090-public-20261112 agg (mean of 8), Arc xpub-curve-20261112 (+r2) prose/code mean, Arc prefill factor from the 32k quiet-rerun prefill (2,823 tok/s, xquiet-prefill-20261113; tasksim-quietprefill-20261113.out); per-request waits from the agent_replay rerun at today's KV sizes. Calibration: ours on the RTX 5090 models 1.18 min median vs 2.02 min measured from the trace.

ram_tier._note: shared RAM-tier pool (llmt-kvbroker); 186 x 3,200 tokens is an upper bound (GDN-state entries share the slots)

on_demand._note: Hot loading of the vision encoder (mmproj) and LoRA adapters (2026-11-13). Tower size and source copy time from the engine logs (LAZYVIS, both GPUs); KV bytes per token = KV cache bytes / tokens of today's production engines (RTX 5090 8.14 GiB / 439,476; Arc 54.8 MiB per 3,200-token block); LoRA lending from the Arc lab (2026-11-13: 1 adapter slot row = 5 KV blocks = 16,000 tokens; 3 rows = 14 blocks = 44,800 tokens). LoRA is tested, not yet in production.

memory_pool._note: RTX 5090 memory budget (GiB) from engine logs + the memory-lending design (2026-11-13). 'reserved' = fixed reserves sized for peaks: activation reserve 2.08, vision encoder resident 0.86, LoRA slots (3 adapters) 0.8, margin left unused 1.43. Pool design: KV takes everything except weights, graphs and a fixed floor; elastic tenants borrow KV blocks (coldest first, copies in the RAM tier). Gains per GPU from the analysis: Arc ~+110k tokens (+22 %), 5090 ~+130-155k (+30-35 %). Status 2026-11-13: LoRA + encoder lending lab-tested on the Arc, packed KV pool validated on the 5090, scheduler-moved prefill boundary in progress.
